title: Emojis: A New Language? Nah.
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the history of emojis, starting with text emoticons: Scott Fahlman's 1982 smiley-face post on a Carnegie Mellon message board, and a possible earlier emoticon in Robert Herrick's 1648 poem. They cover NTT DoCoMo's 1999 pager icons in Japan, engineer Shigetaka Kurita's i-mode emoji set and the coining of the term "emoji," and the 2010 Unicode Consortium standardization. They discuss emoji as language versus art (Emoji Dick, Young Jake portraits), linguist Rachel Tatman's picture-ordering study, Vyv Evans's views, the Oxford Dictionary word-of-the-year choice, controversies (cheeseburger, eggplant and peach, skin tones, emoji threats and arrests), the Emoji Movie, and upcoming Emoji 11.0 and 12.0 proposals. The episode ends with a Meals on Wheels listener mail segment and sign-off.
topics: Oxford word of the year crying laughing emoji

segments.title: Opening banter and bitmoji
segments.summary: Hosts joke about their bitmoji avatars, texting habits like thumbs-up and 'k' replies, and introduce emojis as modern hieroglyphs.

segments.title: Emoticons and early smiley faces
segments.summary: Scott Fahlman's 1982 smiley-face post on a Carnegie Mellon message board, the purpose of marking jokes, and a claimed earlier emoticon in Robert Herrick's 1648 poem.

segments.title: Pagers and DoCoMo's first emojis
segments.summary: NTT DoCoMo's Pocketbell pagers in Japan added heart and phone icons in 1999; business users objected, and teenagers moved to other services. The hosts explain how pagers worked.

segments.title: Shigetaka Kurita and i-mode
segments.summary: Engineer Shigetaka Kurita created about 176 to 276 emoji for the i-mode mobile platform under a character limit, storing images on the phone and triggering them by short codes; he coined the term emoji.

segments.title: Unicode standardization
segments.summary: The Unicode Consortium, a nonprofit, standardized emojis around 2010 so they display consistently across platforms; no one owns them, though tech companies have outsized influence and the set skews American.

segments.title: The Emoji Movie and crying-laughing emoji
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the Emoji Movie as a result of free emoji use, and the crying-with-laughter emoji being named Oxford's word of the year, which they feel is overused.

segments.title: Tone, punctuation and workplace emoji use
segments.summary: Discussion of how text lacks tone, how punctuation like periods and exclamation points carry meaning, and a 2017 study finding many smiley emojis reduce perceived competence.

segments.title: Eggplant, peach, poop and cheeseburger controversies
segments.summary: Emoji sexual connotations (eggplant and peach), the poop emoji with Google eyes, the cheeseburger design outcry, and a survey linking emoji use to sex.

segments.title: Skin tones, emoji threats, and emoji as language
segments.summary: Skin tone options introduced in 2015, arrests for emoji threats, emoji art portraits, Emoji Dick translation of Moby Dick, and linguistics debate including Rachel Tatman's picture-ordering study and Vyv Evans's view of emojis as a new communication form.

segments.title: Upcoming emojis: Emoji 11.0 and 12.0
segments.summary: Unicode released proposed Emoji 11.0 and planned Emoji 12.0 with disability-related icons; the hosts discuss upcoming designs like the clown face and super villain.

segments.title: Meals on Wheels listener mail
segments.summary: A listener says an earlier Meals on Wheels episode inspired him to volunteer in Columbus, Ohio. The hosts close with contact info.
